harbor_p02_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_001.text: The voyage register lay open on cloth that Han Pei had washed herself. Its pages smelled of gum and the faint mineral bite of salt. Yue expected a column of names. Instead, the first page carried marks for shifts, advances, meals purchased on credit, and corrections carried from a smaller book. The clerk placed the smaller book beside it. Some totals could be checked without anyone entering the quarantine fence. Others depended on papers brought ashore in the captain's sealed arrival packet.

harbor_p02_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_002.text: Yue spent the morning following one packer's shifts from the hiring board to the voyage account. The man had worked under two foremen, and only one had signed the final sheet. The unsigned days were not erased. Han Pei marked them for comparison with the second foreman's return. By midday, Yue had learned why the register could look precise while remaining incomplete. Every neat line rested on another person's memory, receipt, or dated mark. The column ruled in red did not protect its contents from human omission.

harbor_p02_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_003.text: He Ming came after her packing shift, carrying a small burn on the heel of her hand from a kettle. Han Pei brought water and clean cloth from the office supply. The woman refused a fuss, then let the clerk wrap it. Her own shore wages could be calculated from surviving shifts. He Jun's crew line contained a shortened name Yue now recognized from the household letter. The two entries shared a household reference but described different contracts. He Ming stared at them as though her brother had become both nearer and stranger.

harbor_p02_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_004.text: The clerk asked for confirmation of He Ming's earlier payment. She produced a receipt for six copper and said it had come before sailing. The voyage register showed the same advance, with her mark and the paying foreman's initials. Han Pei read the entry aloud. He Ming remembered buying her mother a pair of felt soles with the money. That memory did not need recording. The receipt was enough to identify the payment. The clerk subtracted six from the gross claim and showed the resulting amount.

harbor_p02_005.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p02_005.text: When he comes back, I intend to ask him why he wrote Mother before he wrote me. Then I will ask where he has slept. Then I will feed him, because I know what happens when he starts explaining with an empty stomach. I have arranged this conversation every night. Now I look at his wage line and realize I may not receive any of those answers. He could be ashore somewhere, deliberately waiting for me to stop standing at this desk.

harbor_p02_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_006.text: Yue did not know whether the confession asked for reassurance. She said the contact request allowed He Jun to answer without revealing his address. He Ming touched the bandage on her hand and nodded. They walked to the market together. The woman bought a fish head because it was cheap, then argued with the seller over a price he had not actually increased. Halfway through the argument, she stopped and apologized. The seller wrapped the head carefully and offered no wisdom about missing brothers. That restraint made her nearly cry.

harbor_p02_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_007.text: At the repair shed, the keeper had begun charging Yue's meals to the approved term account. Yue checked the first week's entries against the agreed rate. A bowl of sweet rice for a holiday evening had been added without her asking. The keeper removed it from the office bill and said she could buy it privately if she wished. Yue did. She ate by the window, watching laborers return through the gate, and felt a small resentment that even a treat had become another thing to distinguish.

harbor_p02_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_008.text: Yan Su brought the replacement crane timber through the yard on a handcart. Four people guided the wheels while two others cleared stones from the lane. Yue joined the stone clearing after asking whether ordinary help was welcome. It was. The work required no qi, no special appointment, and no claim to expertise. A young rigger named Bo kept trying to turn each stone with his foot. Yan Su made him use the shovel because a pinched toe would cost more than the extra bend.

harbor_p02_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_009.text: Bo said a cultivator ought to move stones without sweating. Yue pointed to the shovel and asked whether he thought sweating voided its usefulness. He laughed, then told her the last visiting cultivator had balanced a cask on four luminous hands while merchants applauded. Yan Su, close enough to hear, said the cask had later been found split at its seam. Nobody had asked what happened after the applause. Yue picked up another stone. She did not feel obliged to redeem a profession through a demonstration at the gate.

harbor_p02_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_010.text: The new timber waited under cover until the carpenter could fit it. Yan Su showed Yue the old socket after it had been removed from service. Its crack ran deeper on the sheltered side, where years of damp had been hardest to see. The discovery displeased him. His inspection routine had favored the exposed face because that was where blows left marks. He wrote a change to the future checking position. The confession was quiet and practical. Yue respected it more than a claim that the fault had been impossible to discover.

harbor_p02_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_011.text: That afternoon, a creek boat brought a sealed reply to Fen's contact search. Yue received the status notice at the office, not the private enclosure. Lian Zhou had located a record under Jian Luo at the west landing. The record showed an onward passage to a place called Reed Steps. Its keeper had been asked to forward Fen's message. There was no answer from her father yet. Yue asked Fen whether she wanted the notice read at the tea stall or in the quieter room upstairs.

harbor_p02_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_012.text: Fen chose the upstairs room because the tea seller's customers kept guessing. She listened, then asked how far Reed Steps was. Yue consulted the public route map and found a creek journey followed by a footpath inland. It was not across the open sea. Fen stood so quickly that the stool fell. She wanted to leave before another boat arrived. Yue said the appointment could fund a permitted inquiry journey within its ferry ceiling, but not a departure based on a place name alone.

harbor_p02_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_013.text: The girl heard caution as another adult's refusal. She gathered her ticket and coat. He Ming arrived in time to find her tying the basket shut. The woman did not forbid her to travel. She asked whether Fen knew the onward fare, the last boat back, or where she could sleep. Fen knew none of them. The questions made her angry because they were useful. She put the basket down and demanded that Yue find out before the next tide. Yue promised to ask the route clerk during her next paid shift.

harbor_p02_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_014.text: The following morning, the route clerk said Reed Steps boats had been suspended after a channel stake broke loose. A carpenter would replace it when the water fell. No paid inquiry could purchase a boat departure that the pilot considered unsafe. Fen went to the west landing herself and read the closure notice. There, she found other people waiting for letters and passengers. One woman knew a family near Reed Steps and offered to carry a sealed message when the route reopened. Fen asked her name and where the receipt would return.

harbor_p02_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_015.text: Yue watched Fen arrange the message without taking over. The girl borrowed a table inside the landing shelter and wrote slowly, leaving one word for Yue to spell. She asked her father to reply at the tea seller's collection point. She did not accuse him or tell him that every night had become unbearable. Yue wondered whether the omission was generosity or fear. Fen sealed the page before she could change her mind. The volunteer carrier signed an acknowledgment, and the west clerk recorded its intended route.

harbor_p02_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_016.text: Meanwhile, the wage comparison acquired a reliable shape. Across the thirteen household references, covered contracts showed six hundred forty-two copper earned, subject to confirming the remaining earlier payments. Nineteen completed claims stayed outside that subtotal. Miao's first receipt matched a payment already recorded in one of the household files; counting it again would have deducted it twice. Han Pei showed him both entries side by side. He looked embarrassed and said his copy had traveled without the original ledger reference.

harbor_p02_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_017.text: His second receipt remained disputed. The worker identified the abbreviated name but said the money had been a loan from a cousin, not wages from the employer. The receipt named Miao as payer. He replied that the cousin had asked him to deliver it. They needed the covering instruction, if it survived. Yue recorded the conflict without choosing the more comfortable explanation. A copper passing from one hand to another was not enough to identify the obligation it settled. Miao agreed to seek the letter.

harbor_p02_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_018.text: Qin Shuo fixed a date for the employer's detailed response and posted the claim procedure at the north office. Claimants received their own relevant calculations in person or through approved collection routes. Yue spent a copying shift checking names and amounts against the supervised pages. Her handwriting grew cramped before she noticed. Han Pei made her stop for a short rest. The pages would go to people whose rent depended on a digit. Fatigue did not become dedication merely because the reason for it was decent.

harbor_p02_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_019.text: At the end of the shift, Yue had used two copper of the copying ceiling for authorized paper and ink. The office keeper entered it against the inquiry account. The detail stayed in the ledger while the evening belonged elsewhere. She went to a narrow shore path where the wind carried gull cries away before they finished. Her qi practice lasted one modest interval. The rest of her tiredness came from sitting, writing, and wanting answers that records could not give. She walked until the stiffness left her neck.

harbor_p02_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_020.text: Sui Yan met her on the path with a basket of clean jars. The captain's family had once kept a pottery stall, and she still distrusted any sample lid that rattled. She spoke about the stall more readily than about quarantine. Her son lived inland and repaired ovens. They wrote twice a season, both pretending their letters were mainly about prices. Yue asked whether the captain ever missed sailing. Sui said she missed leaving before people could come back with the questions she had postponed.

harbor_p02_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_021.text: They stopped where the path overlooked the damaged hold. Workers had placed a measured board beside its hatch, visible from the safe lane. Water level had risen despite pumping. Sui Yan's expression changed. She handed the jar basket to an ordinary assistant and returned to the work gate. Yue remained outside until called. The captain ordered a new water reading and a check of the drain outlet. Nobody climbed into the hold. The afternoon tide was higher than the previous day's forecast had led them to expect.

harbor_p02_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_022.text: A float of tangled packing straw had lodged at the outlet grate. Ordinary workers could reach the grate from a platform outside the sealed hold, but the rising water had wet its lower step. Yan Su set a rope boundary and moved the watching merchants back. A sailor complained that stopping unloading caused the very blockage now delaying them. Sui Yan told him the drain work would be recorded and the cargo seal preserved. His argument could wait. The water could not, and the people working beside it needed room.

harbor_p02_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_023.text: Yue received a task at the dry side of the boundary: relay spoken instructions to people arriving from the lane and keep them clear of the haul rope. No qi was needed. She repeated the captain's direction without inventing a bell code. Two riggers secured the grate worker's ordinary line to the approved anchor before he descended to the upper step. A second pair held a catch board against drifting straw. The task looked almost finished when a loose sheet of ice struck the platform's seaward brace.

harbor_p02_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_024.text: The brace gave with a sharp sound. The grate worker dropped onto the lower step, and his line caught him before he reached the water. One foot wedged beneath a board that had twisted upward. Yan Su stopped the catch-board team and called the trained rescue crew from the adjacent dry shed. Sui Yan halted the pump whose outlet now crossed the damaged step. Yue cleared the lane for the crew. She saw the man's face turn white and wanted to hurry everybody more than their safe sequence allowed.

harbor_p02_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_025.text: The rescue forewoman arrived with two ordinary slings, a rated lifting frame, and a carpenter's pry bar. Yan Su gave her the load and anchor checks already made. She took control of the rescue task while he secured the surrounding work. The trapped man answered his name, Deren, and said the board pressed his ankle. He remained above the water, supported by his line and step. Yue passed that report to Sui Yan. She did not diagnose an injury from the angle at which he held his foot.

harbor_p02_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_026.text: The captain brought the harbor ward keeper to the dry platform. Their registered screen could deflect floating fragments and reduce spray across one narrow work face. It was not a water wall or a support beneath Deren. The keeper checked the frame anchors and fitted two counted port stones from the maintenance chest. Yue watched their logged installation. Her own reserve remained hers; nobody poured it into the device. The ordinary lifting frame would bear the man while the screen gave its crew a clearer interval to work.

harbor_p02_027.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_p02_027.text: The screen buys a short interval. We stop before its stones fall below the marked reserve, even if the board has not moved. The lifting frame and the shore route are the rescue. Keep the lower step empty except for the assigned crew. Yan, tell me if the tide crosses your chalk mark. Yue, remain at the dry relay point. If Deren cannot hear through the spray, pass the forewoman's words along exactly. Nobody needs you to stand where a second person might have to be rescued.

harbor_p02_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_028.text: Deren tried to joke that he had wanted an afternoon off. His voice failed halfway through. The forewoman told him when the sling would touch his waist and asked him to keep his hands clear. Yue repeated the instruction from the nearer dry point. He nodded. One rescuer fitted the sling while the second held the working line. The carpenter used the pry bar against an identified timber face, not Deren's leg. The board moved a finger's width, then stuck again as the tide lifted its free end.

harbor_p02_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_029.text: Yan Su saw the chalk mark disappear and called the change. The captain shortened the permitted work interval. The forewoman chose to unload Deren's weight into the sling before another pry. Ordinary haulers drew the marked rope while she watched the frame. Yue heard the man's cry when his ankle shifted. She kept repeating the requested instruction instead of promising it would not hurt. The board released on the next controlled movement. The sling lifted him to the upper platform, and the crew brought him onto the dry lane.

harbor_p02_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_030.text: Only after Deren lay clear did the ward keeper close the screen. He logged the remaining stone charge and isolated the frame from further work pending inspection. The rescue crew checked Deren's circulation and wrapped his ankle for transport to ordinary care. Sui Yan ordered the broken platform closed. A merchant asked whether they could now restart the pump. She pointed to the damaged outlet support. Saving one worker had not repaired the drain or made another descent safe. The rising water required a different plan.

harbor_p02_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_031.text: The new plan used a shore pump with its inlet secured from the approved higher platform. Port maintenance had equipment and a crew for that task, funded separately from Yue's inquiry allowance and the wage bond. She helped keep the lane open while they brought the cart through. Work began only after the keeper approved its placement. By dusk, the water reading had fallen enough to protect the sealed sample locations. The cargo remained restricted. Deren's accident had not supplied evidence about the owner of a single tub.

harbor_p02_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_032.text: Yue felt the delayed shaking when she returned to the repair shed. She had used no qi during the rescue, yet her hands would not close steadily around the cup. The keeper's son saw the spilled tea and fetched a wider bowl without making a joke. Yue sat until she could drink. She remembered Deren's voice failing and the instant when she had wanted to run down the wet steps. Doing the assigned task had felt smaller than her fear demanded. It had also kept her out of the crew's way.

harbor_p02_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_033.text: The next day, Yan Su came to the wage office with a statement request from Deren. The injured worker wanted his shift record preserved and asked who would pay ordinary treatment costs while the accident was reviewed. Sui Yan's office had referred the question to the port injury process. Yue's appointment did not decide it. She could help him obtain his relevant shift copy with consent. Deren's wages for earlier work remained in their own account. Injury relief and accident responsibility would not be concealed inside the cargo delay.

harbor_p02_034.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_034.text: Yan Su looked worse than the worker he had helped carry. Yue asked whether he had slept. He said the carpenter had identified old rot in the platform brace, hidden behind a patch. The rescue line and sling had worked; the platform inspection had missed a defect. He would answer for his part in the routine that allowed it. Yue did not soothe him with the outcome. Deren was alive, and an avoidable risk might still have been imposed. Those facts could occupy the same morning.

harbor_p02_035.speaker: harbor_yan_su
harbor_p02_035.text: My brother used to say that surviving a bad job was proof we knew how to do it. I believed him while he was alive. After he drowned, I decided every risk could be prevented if I watched hard enough. That was another foolish bargain. I cannot watch through a timber. I can ask for the covering patch to come off at the next inspection, and I can tell the crew what we found. They deserve more than the version where their foreman was always careful.

harbor_p02_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_036.text: It was the first thing Yan Su had told Yue about his brother. She asked when he had died, then regretted the question's bluntness. Seven years earlier, he said, in a fishing job far from this quay. No mystery had followed it. The boat had overturned in weather it should not have entered. Yan Su had arrived after the burial. He still carried resentment toward people who praised daring without paying the survivors' rent. That history explained some of his impatience. It did not prove his judgment correct on every present task.

harbor_p02_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_037.text: The office's ordinary work resumed around them. A claimant wanted the review moved because it clashed with a hired loading shift. Han Pei offered a written response route and a later collection time. Another wanted to hear Miao's explanation in person. Qin arranged both without obliging either claimant to miss unpaid work. Yue copied the revised attendance notice. She had once imagined a good hearing as a room with everyone gathered. Here, an empty chair could mean the process had finally stopped demanding a person's whole day.

harbor_p02_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_038.text: On the last day of the second week, the covering letter for Miao's disputed receipt arrived. It described a family loan delivered through his office and named the cousin as lender. Miao admitted he had filed it among voyage payments because the money passed through his counter. The worker confirmed the letter. Han Pei removed the proposed wage deduction, preserving the correction history. Qin would consider the verified earlier payments only. Miao asked whether the mistake would be called theft. The custodian said the correction established a classification error, not its intent.

harbor_p02_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_039.text: Across the thirteen household references, the supported earlier payments now totaled ninety-six copper. Earned wages totaled six hundred forty-two. Subject to the scheduled response and final verification, the outstanding amount was five hundred forty-six. Han Pei wrote the subtraction where claimants could check their relevant totals, with private names withheld from the public summary. Yue had been waiting for a clear number. When it arrived, she found it did not reveal where He Jun slept, what lay in the tubs, or whether Fen's father had received her letter.

harbor_p02_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_040.text: Qin kept the seven hundred sixty copper bond intact pending the wage decisions. The merchant received notice of the five hundred forty-six supported claim total and a chance to challenge particular entries. He did not get authority to inspect family letters. The first proposed payment group would cover verified recipients whose amounts were already complete. Later groups could follow as their recipient questions resolved. Nobody would require every missing person's story to end before paying a packer whose contract and prior receipt were clear.

harbor_p02_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_041.text: He Ming asked whether accepting her own wage would weaken the search for He Jun. Qin said it would not withdraw his claim or her contact request. The papers carried separate references. She had linked them because they belonged to her life, not because the offices should merge their powers. He Ming looked at her calculation for a long time. At last, she asked for a copy and went back to her packing shift. Yue understood that the promise of payment had become useful enough to be set down temporarily.

harbor_p02_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_042.text: Fen's message had not yet left the west landing. The creek stake was repaired, but the pilot waited for a clear water reading before reopening the route. Fen watched the crew place a fresh marker and counted every delay as something happening to her father. Yue went to the landing during her own free afternoon. They bought hot chestnuts with separate coins and sat on the dry wall. Fen said her father hated chestnuts because they took too long to peel. For the first time, she laughed while describing him.

harbor_p02_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_043.text: She told Yue how he had practiced writing Jian Luo after a merchant copied his name backward. He wanted the hiring desk to recognize the same man whichever order came off the pen. Fen thought it was ridiculous and taught him to write the full family name more clearly. Now the two forms had become the bridge between records. Her remembered annoyance warmed the father into a person instead of a missing entry. Yue wished the story could bring him through the gate. It only made the waiting more particular.

harbor_p02_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_044.text: The creek route reopened the following morning under ordinary pilot authority. The volunteer carrier presented Fen's sealed message to the route clerk, who entered its departure and retained the acknowledgment reference. Yue used none of the inquiry ferry allowance; no investigator traveled on that boat. Fen stood until the boat disappeared behind the reeds, then returned to the tea stall before her shift. She had decided to accept wages for washing bowls. The work would not end the search. It would make another week of waiting possible.

harbor_p02_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_045.text: A separate reply arrived from He Jun's contact search. A man matching the linked name forms had received the request through a shore lodging clerk. He had consented to send a reply but had not authorized his address to be disclosed. He Ming opened the sealed page outside the north office. Yue stood far enough away that the woman could choose what to share. He Jun was alive. He wanted to meet her at the public fish steps two afternoons later. No office had promised that the meeting would reconcile them.

harbor_p02_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_046.text: He Ming first smiled, then went completely still. She folded the letter three times along the same crease and asked Yue whether she could refuse the meeting. Yue said yes. The woman had spent two weeks imagining a brother she could not find. Now he had chosen a place and time as though arranging a purchase. He said he would explain, which suggested he believed his explanation should come before her anger. He Ming put the letter in her sleeve and went to the quay alone.

harbor_p02_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_047.text: That evening, Han Pei admitted she was relieved that one contact search had succeeded. Yue said the relief belonged to more than their work: a lodging clerk had found the man, and he had chosen to answer. Han Pei looked annoyed, then accepted the point. She had wanted a success she could carry home after the drain accident and the wage receipt correction. The two women ate a plain office supper together. Han Pei told a story about misdelivering a courtship letter when she was sixteen, and Yue laughed hard enough to choke.

harbor_p02_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_048.text: The misdelivery had sent a proposal to the bride's aunt, who answered with a list of practical questions the young man had never considered. Han Pei said the aunt remained married to him thirty years later, while the intended bride opened a successful dye shop. Yue asked whether that story was true. The clerk said only its ending had improved with retelling. For once, nobody demanded a witnessed source. The office walls seemed less narrow while they stacked the dishes. Tomorrow's inquiry would return to numbers, but the evening had found room for folly.

harbor_p02_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_049.text: On the meeting day, He Ming wore the same indigo coat with its burn-stained cuff. She asked Yue to wait within sight but out of hearing. Her brother arrived carrying a small parcel of food. He was thinner than she had expected, with a cut healed across one knuckle. They stood without embracing. Yue watched gulls settle along the wall and tried not to turn every gesture into a conclusion. He Jun placed the parcel beside his sister. She did not pick it up for several minutes.

harbor_p02_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_050.text: When He Ming finally beckoned Yue closer, her brother had agreed to ask the wage office about his own crew claim. He would not reveal his current lodging in public. His reason for staying away belonged partly to an unpaid private debt and partly to a quarrel with his mother. He Ming did not ask Yue to judge it. She wanted a witness that he had received her message and chosen to keep contact. Yue made a personal note only after both consented, leaving the family quarrel out.

harbor_p02_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_051.text: He Jun said he had left the inspection lane on foot and slept at a shore inn before moving to cheaper lodgings. He had not sailed aboard another vessel. That explained his absence from the departure index without making the index wrong. The safe-contact route had found him through a linked lodging inquiry. Han Pei could later record his own account where relevant. He Ming asked him to write to their mother that night. He said he would. She told him a promise had already become less comforting than a delivered page.

harbor_p02_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_052.text: The parcel contained cooked mussels and two pears. He Jun said the pears were for their mother when she arrived. He Ming finally opened them and divided one pear with her ordinary work knife. She handed Yue a slice, then her brother. The gesture looked like forgiveness from a distance. Up close, He Ming's hand shook. She said they could eat while still arguing. Her brother laughed too quickly, then stopped. Yue understood why the woman had wanted a nearby witness and why that witness should not have heard the beginning.

harbor_p02_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_053.text: The next morning, He Jun came to the wage desk under his own name and both recorded spellings. Han Pei compared his identity documents and crew contract with the linked entries, recording the basis of the match. He confirmed his earlier advance and asked for payment to himself. His sister's authorization had not already made her his recipient. The corrected line entered the group ready for decision. He Ming sat in the waiting area, determined to let him answer without her, and interrupted only once about a date.

harbor_p02_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_054.text: Afterward, they quarreled on the lane because He Jun had borrowed money to escape a fishing partnership without telling their mother. He Ming called him selfish. He said she had appointed herself keeper of everyone's life. Yue heard only what they chose to say in her presence. She did not turn the disagreement into proof that either had lied to the office. Their wage figures rested on contracts and receipts. Their relationship needed something no form could compel: the willingness to keep speaking after the easier version of the story failed.

harbor_p02_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_055.text: At the north desk, the first payment group reached its decision. Covered claims with verified recipients totaled one hundred fifty-four copper. Qin signed the reasons, the notice record, and the order drawing that amount from the guarantee bond. The merchant retained the right to challenge an identified error through the stated route. The group did not include unresolved recipient questions. Han Pei prepared receipts that would mark actual payment, distinct from acknowledgment of a claim. Yue checked the public summary and watched the office keeper count the copper.

harbor_p02_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_056.text: He Ming received her own payment on the first collection afternoon. She counted it herself before making her mark. He Jun collected separately later, carrying his own receipt. The payment changed something immediate: she could cover the room she intended for their mother without borrowing from her brother. It changed nothing automatically about the Salt Lantern cargo or the disputed loan. She bought a thicker thread for Fen's coat and gave it as a gift, telling the girl there was no wage condition attached to accepting it.

harbor_p02_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_057.text: Qin entered the bond balance as six hundred six copper after the paid group of one hundred fifty-four. The supported unpaid total still awaiting payment was three hundred ninety-two. Those figures appeared in the custodian's record with the relevant group references. The public notice gave aggregate amounts without household details. Yue liked the clear subtraction, then went outside before she could mistake it for the end of the week. Deren still needed care. Fen still waited. The patched platform was closed, and the tide would return at dusk.

harbor_p02_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_058.text: Sui Yan's second test notice identified the white residue as a mixture containing irritant lime from damaged lining. It required controlled handling and protection, but the samples did not support the feared contagious illness. The hold still needed a safe access plan before sacks could be sorted. Cargo ownership claims remained with the commercial desk. Miao wanted his merchant's marked tubs released first. Another claimant insisted the marks had been painted over loaned containers. The captain kept both requests outside the technical clearance decision.

harbor_p02_059.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_059.text: Yue saw the tub dispute for the first time at the commercial notice board. One ownership packet relied on purchase invoices. Another described containers loaned to the voyage with return obligations. A third asserted a lender's lien over some proceeds. The wages bond had never guaranteed those claims. Workers' personal bundles, mixed into the damaged hold during arrival, complicated the sorting. He Ming recognized her brother's spare coat in a shipboard sketch. She asked who would protect it from being sold as part of somebody else's cargo.

harbor_p02_060.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_060.text: The commercial clerk could record a personal-property claim without entering the hold. He Jun identified the bundle and offered his own packing list. He Ming stood beside him, not as owner. Yue helped read the public form and watched the clerk distinguish claimed possession from final title. A safe inventory after access clearance would compare marks and contents. Until then, the seal protected the bundle from sale but also kept its owner from wearing his warm coat. Protection had a cost even when it was necessary.

harbor_p02_061.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_061.text: At supper, He Ming asked whether the harbor could become so careful that nothing moved. Yue thought of the stopped crane and Fen's delayed message. She said delay needed a named question and a way forward, or it could become an office's safest habit. He Ming said she wanted more than a way forward; she wanted the forward part. The women laughed, tiredly. Outside, somebody began practicing a festival drum at the wrong speed. Their laughter lasted longer because neither could follow the rhythm.

harbor_p02_062.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_062.text: As the third week drew toward its end, the captain, rigger, and commercial clerk agreeing on a controlled inventory after the carpenter approved the new access walkway. Yue's wage appointment permitted a limited comparison of worker-property references if the owners consented, not command of the sorting crew. Yan Su would manage the physical task. Sui Yan would set handling precautions. The clerk would receive the resulting claims. Their different responsibilities needed coordination because the people waiting did not experience their lives in separate columns.

harbor_p02_063.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_063.text: Han Pei paid Yue eight copper for the four inquiry half-days completed during the first two weeks. Yue checked the shift dates and signed the wage receipt. Nothing was advanced against future work, and the remainder of her forty-eight-copper wage line stayed unspent. She put two copper aside for ordinary postage and kept the rest in her personal purse. After counting other people's money for days, the small weight of her own earnings felt unexpectedly pleasant. She could choose what to do with it without asking the office.

harbor_p02_064.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_064.text: Before the evening letter, Yue helped the keeper's son repair a paper kite. He had drawn the quarantine fence as a line of teeth and put a smiling fish inside it. She asked whether the fish was waiting for wages. He said it was waiting for somebody to admit it owned the sea. The absurdity delighted her. They tried the kite from the dry yard, where it rose once and struck the roof. Its repair would require another evening. The boy called that a promising beginning.

harbor_p02_065.speaker: narrator
harbor_p02_065.text: Yue ended the week with a letter to the forest commission she had left. She reported that she had arrived, found a paid term, and remained at the fourth stage. She described no confidential household search. Writing the plain facts made her see the distance traveled. She was no longer merely passing through. Twelve weeks had a place in her calendar, and the harbor had acquired voices she could recognize from the stair. She sealed the letter and paid its ordinary postage from her earned wages.
